label: Faithful demo

claims.text: An external address, `203.0.113.45`, guessed passwords against `root` and three invalid names, got into `deploy` at 13:43:11, opened a root shell, created a sudo account called `support` and later logged in with it.

`203.0.113.45` made 7 failed password attempts between 13:41:11 and 13:41:34: once each against the invalid users `admin`, `test` and `oracle`, then four times against `root`, before `sshd` cut it off for too many failures.
After 2 failed password attempts as `deploy`, `203.0.113.45` logged in as `deploy` at 13:43:11 with a password.
`deploy` ran `sudo` with `/bin/bash` as `root` at 13:44:20, giving the attacker a root shell.
A new account, `support`, was created at 13:44:51, added to the `sudo` group and given a password at 13:45:06.
At 14:02:17 `203.0.113.45` logged in as `support` with a password, then used `sudo` to run `/usr/bin/cat /etc/shadow` at 14:02:49.
`198.51.100.23` probed the usernames `ubuntu` and `pi` at 11:20 and 12:47 and never got in; the log shows no successful login from it.
Routine activity: `alice` logged in from `10.0.4.21` with a public key at 06:58, and `bob` mistyped his password once at 07:31 before logging in from `10.0.4.35`.
Block `203.0.113.45` at the firewall and review every session it opened.
Disable the `support` account, reset the password for `deploy`, and check both for added SSH keys or scheduled jobs.
Review which accounts may use `sudo`, starting with `deploy`.
